newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Gresik Q1 results seen lower than forecast.
newsitem.headline: Gresik Q1 results seen lower than forecast.

text.p: Major Indonesian cement maker PT Semen Gresik's earnings in the first quarter of 1997 are widely expected to be around 33 billion rupiah ($13.52 million), sharply lower than a year ago, analysts said on Thursday.

"There is market talk that Semen Gresik's net profit in the first quarter of 1997 will be about 33 billion rupiah, which is far less than its first quarter earnings in 1996 of 41.2 billion rupiah," a research director of one foreign firm said.
"Although the company has indicated it will be about 36 billion rupiah, still it is lower than market expectations," another foreign analyst said.
Semen Gresik officials have already acknowledged that the company's earnings in the 1997 first quarter will be lower than the year-ago period.

"If we compare the first quarter results of 1997 and 1996 as apples to apples, the result of 1997 is slightly lower. But we have to remember it is most likely caused by changes in the depreciation calculation," said one company official, who declined to give other details.
The earnings are likely to be announced on Friday.
Gresik's share prices fell about 10 percent last week and on Monday to a low of 5,300 rupiah on talk of the fall in earnings.

But share prices have since rebounded mildly on bargain-hunting. On Wednesday, Semen Gresik closed 50 rupiah lower at 5,400 rupiah on a modest volume of 748,000 shares. There was no trade on Thursday because of a public holiday.
However, analysts and brokers said investors were likely to downgrade full-year net profit forecasts for the company.
"Generally people in the market are going to revise down their target for Semen Gresik's net profit for 1997," the research director of one foreign brokerage said.
He said that he expected the full-year net profit to be 253 billion rupiah, down from an earlier market consensus of 318.9 billion rupiah with earnings per share at 538 rupiah.
Semen Gresik booked a net profit of 219.27 billion rupiah in 1996 compared with 162.55 billion rupiah in 1995.
The research director said the fair share price for Semen Gresik would be around 5,400 rupiah if the first quarter net profit was 33 billion rupiah.
"It is very difficult to make a valuation because I haven't seen the breakdown. However, I would like to say the fair price would be at about 5,400 rupiah," he said.
Some analysts said they were puzzled why the firm indicated a lower first quarter profit while announcing a sharp rise in sales compared with 1996.
The Semen Gresik official said sales volume was 2.27 million tonnes in the first quarter of 1997 compared with 1.97 million tonnes in the same period in 1996.
The official said the first quarter sales included 100,000 tonnes of cement produced by the Tuban II plant, which is still under trial operation.
"If we look at the sales figures, it looks all right. I think the problem is not in the cement side," said Bart Schothorst, a senior analyst with DBS Securities Indonesia.
He said the weak first quarter result partly reflected stagnant cement prices and interest expenses.
"Also, it is probably caused by a relatively high tax rate because the of differences in accounting policy," he added. ($ = 2,440 rupiah)
